stops.name: Medina, the letters to the kings of the earth
stops.campa: Peace won at Hudaybiyya, the Messenger turns to the wide world. He has a silver seal graven, Muhammad the Messenger of God, and sends emissaries with letters to the great rulers, calling them to the One God: to Heraclius the Roman, to Chosroes of Persia, to the Muqawqis of Egypt, to his old friend the Negus. Heraclius reads and honours the letter; Chosroes tears it and is warned his kingdom shall be torn likewise; the Negus believes. So from the small oasis-state the summons of Islam goes out to the thrones of the age.
stops.quote: In the name of God, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, servant of God and His Messenger, to Heraclius the great one of the Romans. Peace be upon him who follows the guidance. I call you with the call of Islam; accept Islam and you shall be safe.
stops.quote_source: The letter to Heraclius, in Sahih al-Bukhari 7 and Ibn Ishaq

stops.name: Khaybar, the fall of the fortress oasis
stops.campa: Northward the Messenger leads his men against the fortified Jewish oasis of Khaybar, whose towers and date-groves have harboured his enemies. He gives the banner to Ali, saying it goes to one who loves God and His Messenger and whom they love; and Ali, his eye healed by the Prophet's spittle, takes the great fort of Qamus, striking down the champion Marhab. Khaybar falls, and its lands are left to their people as tenants, giving half their harvest. On the way home the true nature of the faith is tested and the community is enriched and secured.
stops.quote: Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves God and His Messenger, and God and His Messenger love him; God will grant victory through his hands.

stops.name: Mu'ta, the martyrs beyond the Jordan
stops.campa: The faith reaches the borders of Rome. Three thousand are sent north to Mu'ta beyond the Jordan against a vast Byzantine and Arab host. Zayd, the beloved freedman, bears the banner and falls; Ja'far takes it and, his hands struck off, clasps it to his breast until he too is slain. God gives him wings in Paradise, and he is called Ja'far of the Two Wings. Abdullah ibn Rawaha falls after. Then Khalid ibn al-Walid takes up the standard and, by a cunning withdrawal, brings the small army home unbroken from an impossible field.

stops.name: Mecca, the Conquest, the idols cast down from the Kaaba
stops.campa: The truce broken, the Messenger comes down upon Mecca with ten thousand, and the city that cast him out falls almost without a sword. He enters as conqueror, his head bowed low upon his camel in humility before God, and grants a general pardon: Go, you are free. Then he comes to the Kaaba where three hundred and sixty idols stand, and strikes them down one by one with his staff, reciting as they topple: Truth has come and falsehood has vanished. The ancient House of Abraham is cleansed at last and given back to the One God.
stops.quote: Truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is bound to vanish.

stops.name: Mecca, Bilal's call to prayer from atop the Kaaba
stops.campa: On the day of the Opening, the Messenger bids Bilal, once the slave crushed on the burning sand, crying One, One, climb upon the roof of the Kaaba itself and call the people to prayer. The freedman's voice rises over the conquered city: God is greatest; there is no god but God. Where the idols stood, the adhan sounds. The proud of Quraysh hear the black man's call ring out from the holiest place, and the world is turned over. So the tortured slave of Mecca becomes the first muezzin above its House.
stops.quote: Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar. I bear witness that there is no god but God; I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.
stops.quote_source: The Adhan (the call to prayer), as first proclaimed by Bilal

stops.name: The valley of Hunayn, pride humbled, victory given
stops.campa: Fresh from the Opening of Mecca, twelve thousand march on the Hawazin, and some are pleased at their own numbers. In the narrow valley of Hunayn the enemy's archers ambush them from the heights and the great host breaks and flees, until only a handful stand about the Messenger. He does not move, calling them by name back to him, and God sends down His calm and armies unseen. The line re-forms, the Hawazin are routed. So the faithful learn that victory is never in their numbers but in God alone. The last of Arabia bows.
stops.quote: God has helped you on many fields, and on the day of Hunayn, when you were pleased with your great numbers, but they availed you nothing... then God sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and the believers.

stops.name: Mount Arafat, the Farewell Pilgrimage and the Sermon
stops.campa: In the tenth year he leads the pilgrimage himself, and on the plain of Arafat, mounted on Qaswa before a great multitude, he preaches his Farewell Sermon. He declares the blood and property of every man sacred as this day; he abolishes the old feuds and usury; he charges them to be kind to women and to hold fast to the Book. Then descends the verse: This day I have perfected for you your religion. Have I conveyed the message? he asks three times, and the crowd answers Yes. O God, bear witness, he says.
stops.quote: O people, verily your blood and your property are sacred and inviolable to one another, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours.
stops.quote_source: The Farewell Sermon (Khutbat al-Wada'), 9 Dhu al-Hijja 10 AH

stops.name: Medina, the last illness in Aisha's chamber
stops.campa: Back in Medina a fever takes him. Too weak to lead, he bids Abu Bakr guide the prayers, and asks to be nursed in the chamber of Aisha, against whose breast he leans. He frees his slaves, gives away the last coins in the house, and warns against making his grave a place of worship. In his final hours he dips his hand in water to cool his face and murmurs of the struggle of the soul departing, and of the highest companions. He raises his finger to the One God, and is gone.
stops.quote: There is no god but God. O God, the highest companions — to the highest Companion.
stops.quote_source: Aisha's narration of the Prophet's death (Sahih al-Bukhari)

stops.name: Medina, the grave beneath the Green Dome
stops.campa: He dies on a Monday in Rabi al-Awwal, in the eleventh year of the Hijra, and grief overwhelms the city; Umar will not believe it until Abu Bakr steadies them all: whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad is dead; whoever worships God, God is living. As he counselled, they bury a prophet where he dies: in the very floor of Aisha's chamber, beside the mosque he raised. Over that spot the ages will lift the Green Dome of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi, and the road that began at the Kaaba of Abraham comes to rest in the earth of Medina.
stops.quote: Whoever used to worship Muhammad, Muhammad is dead; and whoever used to worship God, God is Alive and shall never die.
stops.quote_source: Abu Bakr's address, in Sahih al-Bukhari; citing Quran 3:144
